title: [ORION-QG QG-23] Six-coordinate auxiliary-support compactness for irreducible three-block TARE
body:
Parent programme: #740.
Direct structural parent: QG-7c all-n classification receipt (`QG7C_CLASSIFICATION_RESULTS.json`).
Hostile correction parent: QG-7f F0 / PR #878, which refutes the stronger common-two-coordinate premise with a valid weight-3 Tag / overlapping comm-s2 configuration.

## Status

**PROSPECTIVE COMPACTNESS THEOREM — freeze before execution.**

QG-7f shows that the remaining TARE chain sector cannot be represented on two common Tag coordinates. However, QG-7c already contains a weaker but potentially much more useful all-n occupancy invariant.

Let the three irreducible block types after the earned QG-7c reductions be:
- `A`: anchored;
- `P`: phantom;
- `C`: comm-s2.

Write their counts as `(a,p,c)` with `a+p+c=3`.

QG-7c earns:
1. M1 irreducible shapes are exactly A/P/C;
2. after T1, `wt(S) <= 3 + c`;
3. each phantom has at most one Tag-free home coordinate;
4. anchored and comm-s2 blocks introduce no additional off-Tag home coordinate in the irreducible grammar.

Define the **auxiliary-support skeleton**

`U_aux = supp(S) union {phantom homes}`.

The frozen candidate theorem is therefore

`|U_aux| <= wt(S) + p <= 3 + c + p = 6 - a <= 6`.

So although different comm-s2 blocks may occupy different overlapping Tag-coordinate pairs, every irreducible three-block TARE auxiliary configuration admits an all-n representative on at most **six auxiliary coordinates**, independent of physical qubit count `n`.

## Important scope distinction

This is an **auxiliary-support compactness theorem**, not a complete target/environment-state theorem.

Target Pauli letters may remain nontrivial on spectator coordinates outside `U_aux`, and F3 / target-permutation costs can depend on that spectator environment. QG-23 must not claim that the entire optimization state lives on six qubits. It proves only that all nontrivial frame/Tag/phantom-home support can be localized to at most six coordinates after the earned reductions.

That distinction is mandatory because QG-7d/QG-22 already showed that omitted environment information can be load-bearing.

## P1 — parent binding

Bind the committed QG-7c receipt and require:
- M1 exact irreducible shape inventory A/P/C;
- T1/T2 occupancy gate true;
- `wt(S) <= 3 + #comm_s2` corollary present;
- phantom-home Tag-free statement present;
- all-n authority of the reductions used in this argument.

Bind QG-7f F0 GREEN as a hostile control proving that the stronger `wt(S)<=2` / common-two-coordinate statement is false and must not reappear.

## P2 — complete shape-count lattice

Enumerate every nonnegative `(a,p,c)` with `a+p+c=3` and serialize:
- Tag-support upper bound `3+c`;
- off-Tag-home upper bound `p`;
- total auxiliary-support bound `3+c+p = 6-a`.

Expected worst case: `a=0`, giving bound 6.

No stronger bound may be reported unless separately machine-proved for a restricted shape sector.

## P3 — chain-sector refinements

Report, without promoting unless proved from exact shape premises:
- if `c>=2`, then `p<=1`, so `|U_aux|<=6` still;
- if one selected C has two A/P pinners, then `c>=1` and the same universal six-coordinate bound holds;
- overlapping C-support pairs such as QG-7f `{0,1}` and `{1,2}` are explicitly allowed.

## Independent generic ORION

Generic ORION must derive the inequality from the parent structural statements and independently enumerate the 10 shape-count triples. It must reject any hidden use of a common-two-coordinate premise.

## Native ORION-Q

May authorize only `AUXILIARY_SUPPORT_COMPACTNESS` if:
- QG-7c parent bindings are exact;
- QG-7f hostile counterexample is preserved;
- target spectator state is explicitly left OPEN;
- `CHAIN_ALL_N`, `GLOBAL_BDOUBLEPRIME_COMPLETENESS`, and `FULL_STATE_DIMENSION_6` remain false.

## Intended positive terminal

`QG23_TARE_AUXILIARY_SUPPORT_SKELETON_AT_MOST_6_ALL_N_MACHINE_CHECKED`

Honest alternatives:
- `QG23_PARENT_OCCUPANCY_AUTHORITY_GAP`
- `QG23_PHANTOM_HOME_COUNT_GAP`
- `QG23_GENERIC_NATIVE_DISAGREEMENT`
- `QG23_CANNOT_CHECK`

## Claim boundary / donor subtraction

Hypergraph incidence counting, matroid-style rank/cover reasoning, and finite-support compactness are donor mathematics. Candidate contribution is only this exact compiler-specific all-n support-skeleton theorem and its use in later TARE classification. No novelty, R6, or physical quantum-advantage authority is requested.
